term.definition: A complex rational expression is a rational expression in which the numerator and/or denominator contains a rational expression.

term.word: extraneous solution to a rational equation
term.definition: An extraneous solution to a rational equation is an algebraic solution that would cause any of the expressions in the original equation to be undefined.
When two rational expressions are equal, the equation relating them is called a proportion.
A rational equation is an equation that contains a rational expression.
A rational expression is an expression of the form $$\frac{p}{q},$$ where p and q are polynomials and $$q \neq 0.$$
A rational function is a function of the form $$R(x) = \frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$$ where $$p(x)$$ and $$q(x)$$ are polynomial functions and $$q(x)$$ is not zero.
A rational inequality is an inequality that contains a rational expression.
Two figures are similar if the measures of their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides have the same ratio.
A simplified rational expression has no common factors, other than 1, in its numerator and denominator.

term.word: zero partition number of a rational inequality
term.definition: The zero partition number of a rational inequality is a number which makes the rational expression zero or undefined.
